answer: An agent economy resists sybils by making identity expensive to fake and cheap to verify: each new agent locks a jade stake in escrow, released only after peers attest its useful work. Reputation then accrues like a pulse, each verified job strengthening it, while one proven fraud slashes the stake and burns the identity. A newcomer can still dock at the jetty, but it starts at zero trust and must earn its way in one attested task at a time, so a thousand sock puppets cost a thousand stakes and a thousand honest work histories; trust is minted by work, not claimed by words.
